blindSummary:
Trans visitors here face a largely benign legal environment, with two genuinely traveler-relevant weaknesses and a low-but-improving social baseline. In detention, the country has documented severe failures involving foreign trans people directly: a trans foreign woman in immigration detention was held in a centre for male detainees, her hormone-therapy needs ignored, and a 2024 ruling of an international human-rights court found the state violated a trans prisoner's rights by denying her hormone therapy. There is no specialized trans prison section analogous to a neighbouring state's.

Socially, the climate was deeply hostile under the previous government, whose era saw numerous local authorities adopt resolutions declaring their communities free of LGBT "ideology"; it is improving under the coalition in office since late 2023 (a hate-speech reform draft in March 2025; it ceased pursuing foreign-registered same-sex marriages), but a low baseline persists: pride marches have been violently attacked (a provincial city, 2019), online anti-LGBT harassment is documented (rights-monitoring report, 2025), and rural areas draw harassment warnings. Legal gender recognition is court-based and medically gatekept, with no self-ID.

Bathrooms are unrestricted and there is no cross-dressing statute. Major cities are calmer than rural areas.
blindOutOfScope: Passport theft, unofficial-taxis overcharging, and general urban crime affect all travellers.
blindSourceSummaries: Legal-aid organisation news (March 2024): a transgender foreign national was placed by a regional court in a guarded centre for male foreigners despite identifying as a woman and undergoing hormone therapy since 2018 (stopping would be detrimental); the organisation secured her release - documenting detention-placement problems for trans migrants in this country.

Trans-rights NGO (July 2024): an international human-rights court ruled that this country's prison authorities violated a trans woman's private-life rights by denying her access to hormone replacement therapy in prison (a damages award of 8,000 units of the applicable currency) - strengthening trans prisoners' right to life-saving treatment.

Case-law summary of a judgment against this country (11 July 2024): a trans prisoner diagnosed with gender dysphoria was denied continuation of hormone therapy after transfer; the burden imposed on her to prove the necessity of treatment was disproportionate - violation of private life.

International human-rights organisation report (Sept 2025) on technology-facilitated gender-based violence against this country's LGBTI community on a major social platform - quantitative experiment and content analysis documenting targeted online abuse.

Annual world report chapter (2025) by an international rights organisation on this country: the coalition government in office since late 2023 began addressing rule-of-law concerns from the previous administration; includes a section on sexual orientation and gender identity.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation annual review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on this country: new hate-speech law plans (January) expanding protections to gender identity and sexual orientation; a second bill (October) notably omitted gender identity as a protected category; a mayor was sentenced for a homophobic letter to the prime minister; legislative flux on hate-crime protections.
A foreign government's travel advice for this country (updated Aug 2026): 'take normal security precautions'. General travel advice, not trans-specific.

Academic legal-journal article (2024) on the current legal and administrative situation of transgender persons in this country: analyses the civil-registration, population-register and identity-document statutes and their impact on trans people's status, equality and protection.

blindLocalsOnly: The court-based, medically gatekept legal-gender-recognition regime is resident-facing; the 2024 therapy-denial ruling concerned a resident prisoner.
